title: Jayden Wright — Complete Bodycam and Dashcam Footage — June 26, 2024 — Case 25SL-CR02952

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the The Missouri Sunshine Law, I hereby request the following records:

All body-worn camera recordings, dashboard/in-car camera recordings, and associated audio in the possession, custody, or control of the Missouri State Highway Patrol concerning the entire encounter associated with the following incident:
Individual: Jayden Wright
Incident/offense date listed in Case.net: June 26, 2024
Citation/ticket number: 704435457
Court case number: 25SL-CR02952
Case name: State v. Jayden Wright
Listed charge: DWI, RSMo § 577.010
Listed law enforcement agency: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Troop C — St. Louis
Please provide the complete recordings from every involved trooper, including the primary, assisting, backup, supervising, and transporting troopers—not only the arresting trooper.
The requested scope runs from the earliest recorded observation of or response to this incident through the conclusion of the encounter, including the stop or initial contact, roadside investigation, field sobriety testing, arrest, searches, transport, chemical-testing procedures, processing, and release or transfer of custody, to the extent recorded. Please include any portions of this same encounter continuing into the following calendar day.
Please include all available bodycam and in-car camera views, including forward-facing and rear-seat/passenger-compartment recordings, separately stored audio associated with those recordings, and any retained pre-activation or buffered footage. Please also include any testing-room, interview-room, or booking-area recordings of this encounter held by MSHP.
I am requesting all responsive files and segments from each camera, not selected excerpts, screenshots, summaries, or only footage showing the arrest itself. This request is limited to this incident and does not seek unrelated calls or entire shifts.
Please provide the recordings in their existing electronic format, preserving available audio, timestamps, and recording metadata, subject to legally required redactions. Electronic delivery by download link is preferred; MP4 is acceptable if available. Certified copies are not requested.
If any portion is withheld or redacted, please release all nonexempt portions and provide a written explanation identifying the specific statutory basis for each withholding or redaction.
If no responsive recordings exist or remain available, please indicate, to the extent known, whether recordings were never created, were deleted under a retention policy, or are held by another agency. For any deleted recordings, please provide existing records documenting their deletion and the applicable retention schedule. If another agency holds additional recordings of this encounter, please identify that agency if known.
Please preserve responsive recordings while this request is being processed.
Before incurring any charges, please provide an itemized cost estimate and obtain my written approval. I do not authorize paid processing without that approval.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Will R

title: The City Lending Crisis: DISB Commissioner Communications on Federal Escrow Fraud

communications.communication:

Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

To: claudine.sassa@dc.gov
Cc: lilah.blackstone@dc.gov​, molc.mayor@dc.gov, foia.​appeals@dc.gov
From: Fred Gamble Jr.
Date: September 29, 2026
Subject: D.C. FOIA Request - Formal Submission regarding Commissioner Karima Woods

Dear Claudine Sassa and the DISB Office of the General Counsel,

Pursuant to the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq.), I am submitting a formal request for public records.

Because my prior FOIA requests regarding the Department of Insurance, Securities and Banking's (DISB) oversight of City Lending Inc. were subjected to an administrative default via MOLC Appeal 2026-398, please be advised that this is a legally distinct, highly targeted request based on new federal interventions and title compliance orders that materialized subsequent to my initial filings.

I am requesting the release of the following specific records:

*   All internal emails, memorandums, and briefing documents sent to or from Commissioner Karima Woods generated between January 1, 2020, and the present (September 29, 2026), specifically referencing "HUD OIG Tracking No. 26-FI-HQ-01872", "Stewart Title", or "Do Not Insure" in relation to City Lending Inc. (NMLS: 1045126).  

This request requires a focused search of the Commissioner’s specific communications to establish whether the executive leadership of DISB has been briefed on the active federal investigation and the shattered title insurance associated with this licensee. Because this request relies on a newly issued federal tracking number and a specific secondary market title directive, it cannot be administratively dismissed as a duplicate of any prior request.

I request that you provide these records in their native electronic format, preserving all metadata. If you determine that any portion of these materials is exempt from disclosure under D.C. FOIA statutes, I demand a detailed Vaughn Index legally justifying each specific redaction and explicitly identifying the exemption applied.

Pursuant to D.C. Official Code § 2-532(b), I formally request a waiver of all fees associated with searching, reviewing, and duplicating these records. Disclosure of this information is strictly in the public interest because it will significantly contribute to public understanding of the operations and regulatory activities of the Department of Insurance, Securities and Banking (DISB). This request is made for non-commercial purposes to shed light on whether the District's executive agencies are fulfilling their statutory duties to protect residents from unlicensed financial entities and predatory lending practices. As a Ward 8 resident and community advocate, I am seeking these records to expose a documented federal compliance crisis that directly impacts the safety and financial integrity of the general public.

Given the active nature of the federal investigation (HUD OIG Tracking No. 26-FI-HQ-01872) and the ongoing D.C. Superior Court proceedings this file relates to, time is of the essence. I expect a formal acknowledgment of this request and the commencement of the statutory 15-business-day processing timeline immediately.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Anthropic contracts (General Services Administration)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All contracts, agreements, licenses, subscriptions, task orders, delivery orders, memoranda of understanding (MOUs), memoranda of agreement (MOAs), letters of intent, data-sharing agreements, pilot or proof-of-concept agreements, statements of work, scopes of work, modifications, and other agreement documents between your agency and Anthropic PBC (including any subsidiary, affiliate, or successor entity), or its authorized resellers or cloud distributors acting on Anthropic's behalf (including, but not limited to, Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Palantir Technologies, and Deloitte), that were active or entered into at any time between January 1, 2023, and the date of your search.

These records include, but are not limited to, any agreements relating to Anthropic's Claude products, including Claude, Claude for Enterprise, and Claude for Government, including under GSA's OneGov initiative or GSA Multiple Award Schedule contracts, and any agreements for access to, deployment of, or evaluation of Anthropic's models or services.

For each responsive contract or agreement, I request all documents attached or incorporated by reference, including pricing schedules, usage terms, data protection or data retention terms, acceptable-use or safety restrictions, service-level agreements, security requirements, and any related option or renewal periods.

I also request all records of communications between agency personnel and representatives of Anthropic PBC or its authorized resellers concerning the negotiation, evaluation, pricing, or terms of any such agreement, in any format in which they exist, including email, text messages, and messages on messaging platforms.

If complete contracts are voluminous, I ask that the agency, at minimum, produce:

A list or index of all responsive contracts and agreements, including contract or agreement number, vendor, contracting office, date, period of performance, and dollar value; and
The non-exempt portions of each contract, with redactions limited to the minimum necessary and accompanied by a description of the exemption applied.

Even where an exemption properly applies to part of a record, the statute requires release of all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions. If any document is denied in part or in whole, please specify which exemption(s) are claimed for each passage or whole document denied, and provide a Vaughn index and an itemized inventory of withheld material, specifying the number of pages in each document and the total number of pages pertaining to this request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All electronic mail sent to or received from any email address operating under 
the domain "mcminimeelaw.com" (matching the wildcard string *@mcminimeelaw.com), 
exchanged with any Edmonds School District email account, alias, or internal 
routing node, acting as either the author, sender, primary recipient, 
carbon copy (CC), or blind carbon copy (BCC) holder.

The chronological scope of this request spans the entirety of the District's 
available archival retention window.



TECHNICAL PRE-EXCLUSION OF REPETITIVE SYSTEM DATA:

To maximize administrative processing efficiency, accelerate delivery, and 
eliminate unnecessary review burdens, the requester explicitly waives 
interest in, pre-excludes, and requests the system-level filtering out of 
the following non-substantive records categories:

1. Automated calendar invitations, change notifications, or updates.
2. Automated out-of-office or vacation autoreplies generated by either domain.
3. System-generated IT alerts, ticket confirmations, or password actions.



LIMITATION OF SCOPE & PRE-EXCLUSION OF SENSITIVE DATA:

The requester explicitly pre-excludes and waives any interest in the 
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of any individual student under FERPA.

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.210, if the District asserts that specific internal 
staff names or student indicators are exempt from disclosure, the District is 
required to apply narrow blackouts exclusively to those individual text strings 
while releasing the remaining non-exempt text blocks, financial totals, 
and generalized policy or administrative discussions. 

Blanket withholding of entire records based on broad assertions of privilege 
or exempt status is explicitly contested; only the minimal exempt portions 
may be withheld.



MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:

As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a formal response is required within five (5) 
business days.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

communications.communication:
Re:  NASA FOIA Tracking Number 26-01261-F-HQ

Dear Ms. Green,

This email acknowledges receipt of your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), submitted and received in this office on September 29, 2026. Your request was assigned the above-referenced tracking number.

You seek the following:

"1. Any available list of all entities and individuals that have made requests for press or media credentials, as well as the status of that request, including:

  1.  whether the request was approved or denied
  2.  whether the credential was revoked

2. If no such list exists, please provide all records that reflect all news media and entities that have:

  1.  Applied for press credentials
  2.  Been approved for press/media credentials
  3.  Been denied press/media credentials
  4.  Had press credentials revoked

3. Any directives from the White House regarding the issuance or revocation of press and media credentials."

The FOIA, 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(A)(i), requires NASA to make a determination in response to a FOIA request within 20 business days from its date of receipt. In unusual circumstances, the Federal agency time limit may be extended by 10 business days as stated in 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B). If your request seeks numerous records that will necessitate a wide-ranging search, including searches with components and possible consultations with other entities that have a substantial interest in the determination of this request, NASA will invoke a 10 business day extension for determination of your request. You have the option to narrow the scope of your request to limit the number of potentially responsive records.

Fee Category

In your request, you identify yourself as a member of the news media. NASA FOIA regulations specifically define "representative of the news media" as "any person or entity organized and operated to publish or broadcast news to the public that actively gathers information of potential interest to a segment of the public, uses its editorial skills to turn the raw materials into a distinct work, and distributes that work to an audience." 14 C.F.R. § 1206.507(c)(3)(ii). The FOIA statute also specifically states that to qualify as a "representative of the news media" the person or entity gathering the information must use "its editorial skills to turn the raw materials into a distinct work and distribute that work to an audience." 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(ii). Although you claim that you are a journalistic researcher, your request lacks the information needed to place you in this fee category. If you would like us to re-evaluate your request for media status please demonstrate a solid basis for expecting publication through a news media entity. You may wish to provide a copy of a current publication contract or specific details regarding your past publication record. For this reason, we placed you in the "All Other" request category.

Provisions of the FOIA allow NASA to recover part of the cost of complying with your request. The fees that may be assessed to process a FOIA request vary depending on the category into which the FOIA requester falls. 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(ii)(I),(II),(III). For purposes of fee assessment, you have been categorized as an "All Other" requester. Such requesters are charged for duplication, although the first 100 pages are free; and search time, although the first two hours are free. After that, you will pay $0.15 per page for duplication and the quarter-hour rate of the searcher, plus 16%.  If you disagree with this determination, please provide us with additional information to support the assessment of a different fee category.

Pursuant to NASA FOIA regulation 14 C.F.R. § 1206.504, "submission of a FOIA request shall be considered a firm commitment by the requester to pay all applicable fees charged under this section, up to $50.00." You did not agree to pay any fees; therefore, we will only process your request up to your statutory entitlements of two hours of free search and should our search locate any records responsive to your request, we will only provide you with records up to your statutory entitlement of 100 pages.

Appeal Rights

Because processing is not yet complete, we ask that you defer any appeals until NASA completes its work on your request.  You do, however, have the right to appeal my action regarding your Fee Category request.  Your appeal must be received within 90 calendar days of the date of this letter.  Your appeal must be in writing and addressed to:

title: MPIA Request Regarding Use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) (Baltimore Police Department)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Maryland Public Information Act, I am hereby requesting access to the records listed below and held by the Baltimore Police Department.

1)	Any policies, procedures, protocols, and/or written guidance for the use of Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) by Baltimore Police Department. This request includes, but is not limited to policies setting forth permitted and prohibited uses for ALPRs and rules regarding who may and may not use this technology.

2)	Information about which people and agencies have access to images, videos, and raw data sets generated by ALPR systems monitored or maintained by Baltimore Police Department, under what circumstances these individuals have access to the above-mentioned data, and what information must be entered about any data requests. The list of agencies includes, but is not limited to, parking and traffic enforcement agencies, and other law enforcement agencies.

3)	Policies, procedures and information regarding Baltimore Police Department data retention and data purging practices for ALPR systems, including  Baltimore Police Department policies regarding handling images, videos, and raw data sets.

4)	Information about Baltimore Police Department audits or other procedures used to assure compliance with the above requirements.

5)	Information regarding the training that Baltimore Police Department personnel must undergo to use ALPRs, if any.

6)	ALPR training materials provided to Baltimore Police Department.

7)	Product and user manuals for all ALPR software and hardware possessed or used by Baltimore Police Department.

8)	The name of all ALPR vendors, ALPR software systems, and ALPR hardware currently used by Baltimore Police Department or by third party who make the information available to Baltimore Police Department. Hardware includes fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile devices. Software systems include optical character recognition and artificial intelligence capabilities.

9)	Description of how targets (aka “hot lists”) are shared with ALPR systems and monitored, including the sources for these data feeds.

10)	A list and map of locations where fixed-location ALPRs are currently located within Baltimore Police Department’s jurisdiction.

11)	The number of ALPR devices operated by the agency for the following categories: fixed-location ALPRs, car-mounted ALPRs, and mobile ALPRs.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, please disclose total charges in advance of fulfilling the request. As a result, my request for the above-listed public records is in the public interest. I would prefer the request be filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available, or CD-ROM if not.
